title: Manage scheduled Annals source imports
summary: Queue, prioritize, dispatch, pause, inspect, interrupt, or recover bounded sets of source imports handled through the Annals inbox.
use_when: The configured filesystem inbox, its one-attempt job envelopes, dispatch controls, or bounded retry events must be observed or operated.
A scheduled delivery failure must be diagnosed across Annals domain state and its correlated Nucleus job.
do_not_use_when: One explicitly selected source should be integrated manually.
The proposed recovery edits receipts or archive directories directly.
The desired retry window is omitted, open-ended, or based on future failures.
outcome: A durable and inspectable inbox state transition or report that preserves immutable attempts, archive history, explicit priority, and bounded retry provenance.
effects: Registration moves settled incoming files into durable queued envelopes; direct enqueue copies explicit files and leaves originals unchanged.
Dispatch starts source deliveries and may invoke Nucleus, apply corpus reconciliations, and consume Codex allowance.
The storage gate defers an ordinary claim until the configured reserve is available on both Annals filesystems; direct enqueue rejects a copy that would cross the spool reserve.
Pause blocks new dispatch but permits registration; interruption archives one exact processing job as failed or skipped.
A retry event preserves originals and creates fresh linked child jobs for one frozen inclusive failed-delivery interval.
authority: Annals owns spool envelopes, queue order, priority lanes, source-delivery records, retry events, reconciliation application, and recovery policy.
Nucleus owns only each liaison attempt and its raw runtime records; Nucleus never chooses an Annals retry.
success: Status or event reports identify queue, active job, pause, maintenance, archive, and outcome state without relying on process inspection.
A storage-gated ordinary job remains queued with attempts zero and resumes automatically on a later activation once the condition clears.
A run or retry report, not process exit alone, accounts for every attempted item and durable result.
Original failed jobs and deliveries remain unchanged after retry.
failure_and_recovery: Every inbox job has at most one processing attempt; never move a terminal envelope back to queued.
A storage probe failure prevents a claim and exits nonzero; insufficient storage halts an attended retry until the operator continues it.
When low storage closes the gate, preserve the queued work and leave storage remediation or a reserve change to the user under explicit target-scoped consent.
Unexpected model or runtime failure archives the current job and halts the activation or retry event; continue only through the supported command.
Pause before interruption when the next ordinary job must remain queued, and require paused quiescence before starting or continuing a retry event.
privacy: Inbox envelopes retain unchanged source material and receipts; Annals and Nucleus operational state may retain complete source and model context.
Spool, database, logs, and retry archives belong to the user's private application boundary.
does_not_authorize: Editing spool receipts or moving archived envelopes manually.

Deleting, truncating, pruning, moving, compressing, or otherwise clearing user data as storage remediation, or lowering or disabling the storage reserve, without the user's explicit consent for the exact target and scope.
An unbounded retry or a second attempt for the same job.
Restarting Nucleus while an Annals attempt is active.

consumers.statement: A local Annals operator may observe or operate the configured filesystem inbox, its one-attempt jobs, scheduling controls, interruption, and bounded retry events.
This is not a manual one-work integration path, direct receipt editor, unbounded retry mechanism, or authorization for storage cleanup.

preconditions.statement: Registration, enqueue, and status require the configured private Annals library and spool; dispatch additionally requires available configured reserve, a readable probe, and compatible authenticated Nucleus readiness.
Retry start requires an exact inclusive failed-delivery interval, paused quiescence, no processing job, no unfinished retry event, and no deployment maintenance.
Interruption names one exact processing job, and prioritize or deprioritize names one queued ordinary job.

inputs.statement: Inputs are settled top-level incoming files, explicitly selected regular files, exact job or retry-event IDs, one binary priority lane, and a frozen inclusive failed-job interval.
Open-ended retry, retry-all, terminal-envelope requeue, receipt editing, future-failure selection, and a second attempt for one job are not accepted.

outputs.statement: Status and event reports expose queue, active job, pause, maintenance, archive, attempts, storage gate, retry membership, and durable outcome state.
Registration or enqueue creates complete queued envelopes; dispatch and retry reports correlate jobs with source deliveries and any Nucleus execution while preserving original records.

data_semantics.statement: Registration moves a settled arrival into a queued envelope and direct enqueue copies an explicit file; neither starts a source delivery or creates its database delivery record.
Priority is a binary scheduling lane, not a mutable sequence or corpus property; selection is priority-first then immutable sequence order with no fairness promise.
A closed storage gate is a non-durable dispatch condition that leaves work queued with zero attempts, while pause and maintenance are distinct durable operator and deployment controls.
A retry event preserves original failed jobs and deliveries and creates fresh linked child jobs; it does not give an original job another attempt.

identity_and_units.statement: Job ID identifies one durable spool item, source-delivery ID identifies its Annals processing occasion, retry-event ID identifies frozen recovery membership, and a child job remains distinct from its original.
Queue sequence is immutable and monotonic, attempts are counted from zero to at most one per job, and storage gates compare available bytes with configured reserve bytes on both filesystems.
Retry interval order is ascending failed-delivery completion time with delivery identity as the deterministic tie-break described by Annals.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Status reports current durable spool control and job state for one invocation; a retry event freezes complete eligible membership for its exact inclusive interval at start.
The durable run or retry report, not process exit alone, accounts for every item attempted during that activation or event.
No schedule interval, queue-drain deadline, starvation bound, storage-restoration time, or model-completion latency is promised.

access.statement: The supported boundary is the local Annals inbox CLI and its configured private spool and library; dispatch may use the configured local Nucleus requester interface.
Direct job.json editing, manual archive moves, direct SQLite writes, and host-wide service or storage control are not supported inbox surfaces.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Each job moves from a complete queued envelope to at most one processing attempt and one terminal archive; terminal jobs never return to queued.
A known item-local failure archives that item and ordinary draining may continue, while unexpected model or runtime failure archives the current job and ends the activation nonzero.
Pause prevents the next claim after active work finishes but permits registration; maintenance separately blocks spool mutation and resume clears only pause.
A halted retry continues only its unattempted children and never retries a failed child; original failed history remains unchanged.

operational_limits.statement: Every job has at most one attempt, priority has two lanes, retry membership is an explicit bounded inclusive interval, and ordinary claims require configured free-space reserve on both Annals filesystems.
Low storage is a stop only; this operation cannot clear user data or alter the reserve without separate exact target-scoped user consent.
No queue capacity, maximum file size, throughput, scheduling fairness, or wall-clock completion bound is promised here.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 1, Annals provider release, spool receipt shape, library schema, and Nucleus protocol are separate compatibility axes.
Supported installation and recovery procedures preserve historical envelopes and use product-owned migration rather than manual reinterpretation.
No cross-release spool-format support window or deprecation period is promised.

reliances.statement: Dispatch and retry-child processing rely on Nucleus for authenticated one-attempt model execution and raw runtime records; Annals retains queue, retry, and domain-result authority.
